text.p: The Spanish economy is in a favourable phase, but the nation must continue its policies of fiscal austerity, Luis Angel Rojo, governor of the Bank of Spain said on Thursday.

"The economic situation is fairly favourable. Spain is situated in such a way that it can reasonably aspire to form part of monetary union in the first phase," Rojo said at a seminar on the Spanish economy.
Improvement in inflation and the committment to reducing the public deficit are the elements that will allow the economy as forecast to grow by some 2.7 percent next year, Rojo said.
The Spanish government is forecasting GDP growth of three percent next year.

"The improvement in inflation and the firm commitment of budget policy to public deficit reduction are the main points that will help the economy recovery in the next few months and advance toward the expected levels on the order of 2.7 percent or something similar next year," he said.
